title: Rangpur Dhing Uprising
subtitle: Peasant resistance to revenue collection in Rangpur, 1783
summary: In early 1783, cultivators in Rangpur district rose against revenue demands associated with the East India Company’s revenue farmer Devi Singh. The rebellion, known as the Rangpur Dhing, drew in raiyats and some zamindars; rebel leaders selected Nuruddin as Nawab and Daya Sil as Dewan and organized a levy called dhing kharcha. Historians differ in interpreting the scale and character of the rising.
heroTagline: The 1783 Rangpur Dhing and resistance to revenue exactions
whyItMatters: The Rangpur Dhing shows how revenue farming and coercive collection could provoke organized rural resistance in early Company rule. James Wilson places it within a wider pattern of late eighteenth-century peasant unrest; surviving accounts do not support describing it as a unified nationalist movement.

claimCitations.claim: In early 1783, cultivators in Rangpur district rose against revenue demands associated with the East India Company’s revenue farmer Devi Singh. The rebellion, known as the Rangpur Dhing, drew in raiyats and some zamindars; rebel leaders selected Nuruddin as Nawab and Daya Sil as Dewan and organized a levy called dhing kharcha. Historians differ in interpreting the scale and character of the rising.

The Rangpur Dhing shows how revenue farming and coercive collection could provoke organized rural resistance in early Company rule. James Wilson places it within a wider pattern of late eighteenth-century peasant unrest; surviving accounts do not support describing it as a unified nationalist movement.
